Songpan assistant commander Yao Yu reported: "With Shen Cong I separately reduced Baimalu Shuitu, Ru'er, and other stockades with great success."
57
弘治二年，松潘番寇殺傷平夷堡官軍，命逮指揮以下各官治之。 三年免思曩日安撫等十六族明年朝覲，以守臣言其地方災傷也。 七年，松潘空心寨番賊犯邊，都指揮僉事李鎬敗之。 十三年，番賊入犯松潘壩州坡抵關，勢益獗。 」命逮指揮湯綱等，而敕巡撫張瓚調漢、土官兵五萬，由東南二路分剿，破白羊嶺、鵝飲溪等三十一寨，斬四百余級。 商巴等二十六族皆納款。 十四年復攻黃頭、青水諸寨，前後殺獲男婦七百余人，赭其碉房九百，墜崖死者不可勝計，諸番稍靖。
In Hongzhi 2 Songpan raiders killed troops at Pingyi fort; officers down to the commander were ordered arrested and tried. In year 3 sixteen tribes including Sisangri were excused from next year's audience because local officials reported famine and damage. In year 7 Kongxin stockade raiders crossed the border; regional commander Li Hao defeated them. In year 13 raiders invaded Songpan's Bazhou Podi Pass and grew bolder. The court ordered Tang Gang and others arrested and Zhang Zan to lead 50,000 Han and native troops in two southeastern columns, reducing thirty-one stockades including Baiyang Ridge and E'yin Stream with 400-odd heads. Twenty-six tribes including Shangba's submitted. In year 14 they struck Huangtou and Qingshui stockades, killing or capturing 700-odd people, burning 900 blockhouses, and drowning countless cliff-fallers; the tribes were for a time quiet.
58
嘉靖五年命都督僉事何卿鎮守松潘。 時黑虎五寨及烏都、鵓鴿諸番叛，卿次第平之，降者日至。 卿有威望，在鎮十七年，松潘以寧。 二十三年以北警召卿入衛，繼之者李爵、高岡鳳，未幾皆為巡撫劾罷。 二十六年復命卿往鎮。 時白草番亂，卿會巡撫張時徹討擒渠惡數人，俘斬九百七十余級，克營寨四十七，毀碉房四千八百，獲馬牛器械儲積無算。 終嘉靖世，松潘鎮號得人，邊境安堵焉。 初，龍州薛文勝於洪武六年來降，命仍知龍州。 既置松潘安撫司，命文勝為安撫使。 既置松州衛，仍以松潘為龍州。 宣德七年升龍州為宣撫司，以土知州薛忠義為宣撫使。 龍州者，漢陰平道也。 宋景定間，臨邛進士薛嚴來守是州，捍衛有功，得世襲。 自文勝歸附，其部長李仁廣、王祥皆輸糧餉有功，亦得世襲。 及宣德中，以征松潘功，升州為宣撫使，仁廣為副使，祥為僉事，各統兵五百世守白馬、白草、木瓜番地。 至嘉靖四十四年，宣撫薛兆乾與副使李蕃相仇訐，兆乾率眾圍執蕃父子，毆殺之。 撫按檄兵備僉事趙教勘其事。 兆乾懼，與母陳氏及諸左右糾白草番眾數千人，分據各關隘拒命，絕松潘餉道。 脅僉事王華，不從，屠其家。 居民被焚掠者無算。 是年春，與官軍戰，不利，求救於上下十八族番蠻，皆不應。 兆乾率其家屬奔至石壩，官軍追及之，就擒。 四十五年，兆乾伏誅，籍其家，母及其黨二十二人皆以同謀論斬，余黨悉平。 遂改龍州宣撫司為龍安府，設立流官如馬湖，而割保寧之江油、成都之石泉二縣分隸之。
In Jiajing 5 regional commander He Qing was posted to garrison Songpan. Heihu's five stockades and the Wudu and Boge tribes rebelled; Qing subdued them one by one as surrenders poured in daily. Qing held great authority; after seventeen years at his post, Songpan knew peace. In year 23 northern threats recalled Qing to the capital; Li Jue and Gao Gangfeng followed him in command, but the grand coordinator soon impeached them both from office. In year 26 the court sent Qing back to the garrison. The Baicao tribes rose; Qing and grand coordinator Zhang Shiche took several chiefs, killed or captured 970-odd enemies, stormed forty-seven stockades, razed 4,800 blockhouses, and seized countless horses, cattle, arms, and stores. For the rest of the Jiajing reign Songpan was said to have the right commanders, and the frontier stayed quiet. Longzhou's Xue Wensheng submitted in Hongwu 6 and was left in charge of Longzhou. When the Songpan pacification office was set up, Wensheng became its commissioner. After Songzhou guard was founded, the Songpan region remained Longzhou. In Xuande 7 Longzhou became a pacification commissionerate under native prefect Xue Zhongyi. Longzhou lay on the Han-era Yinping road. Under Song's Jingding reign the Linqiong scholar Xue Yan took the prefecture, defended it with distinction, and won a hereditary post. After Wensheng submitted, chiefs Li Renguang and Wang Xiang earned hereditary posts by supplying grain to the court. For service against Songpan in Xuande the prefecture became a pacification commission: Renguang as vice commissioner and Xiang as assistant, each with 500 hereditary troops on the White Horse, White Grass, and Papaya lands. By Jiajing 44 pacification commissioner Xue Zhaoqian feuded with vice commissioner Li Fan; Zhaoqian besieged Fan and his son and beat them to death. The provincial pacification and surveillance officials ordered border-defense aide Zhao Jiao to investigate. Terrified, Zhaoqian rallied his mother Lady Chen, his retainers, and thousands of Baicao tribesmen to hold the passes, cut Songpan's supply line, and defy the court. He tried to coerce assistant commissioner Wang Hua; when Hua refused, he massacred his family. Countless civilians were burned and plundered. That spring they fought the army and lost; appeals to the upper and lower eighteen fan tribes went unanswered. Zhaoqian fled with his kin to Shiba; troops overtook him there and took him alive. In year 45 Zhaoqian was executed and his property confiscated; his mother and twenty-two accomplices were beheaded, and the rest of the rebels were crushed. Longzhou's pacification commission became Long'an prefecture with regular officials on the Mahu model; Jiangyou of Baoning and Shiquan of Chengdu were detached and attached to it.
59
萬歷八年，雪山國師喇嘛等四十八寨，勾北邊部落為寇，圍漳臘，守備張良賢破之。 犯鎮虜，百戶杜世仁力戰，城得全，世仁死焉。 又犯制臺，良賢復擊之，追至思答弄，連戰大破之，火落赤之侄小王子死焉。 十九年，巡按李化龍言：「松潘為四川屏蔽，疊、茂為松潘咽喉。 番戎作梗，松潘力不能支，宜移四川總兵於松潘以備防禦。 」是時疊、茂諸番眾糾結為亂，鎮巡官率兵剿之，俘馘八百余級，番寇亦斬其部長黑卜、白什等，獻功贖罪。 而松坪諸惡屯據大雪山頂，諸將卒搜討，亦有斬獲。 以捷聞，遂設平武縣於龍安府。
In Wanli 8 the Snow Mountain state preceptor, Lama, and forty-eight stockades joined northern tribes to raid and besiege Zhangla; defender Zhang Liangxian broke the siege. They struck Zhenlu; centurion Du Shiren held the city at the cost of his life. They hit Zhitan next; Liangxian routed them again at Sidalong, killing Huoluochi's nephew the Little Prince. In Wanli 19 touring censor Li Hualong argued: "(Songpan shields Sichuan; Die and Mao are its throat. When the fan tribes stir trouble Songpan cannot hold alone—the Sichuan regional commander should be moved to Songpan for defense. By then Die and Mao fan tribes had risen; garrison and touring officials suppressed them with 800-odd kills, while some fan bands beheaded their own chiefs Heibu and Baishi to buy pardon. Songping's outlaws still held Great Snow Mountain; search columns took heads and prisoners there too. After the victory was reported, Pingwu county was created within Long'an prefecture.
60
松潘以孤城介絕域，寄一線饋運路於龍州，制守為難。 洪武時欲棄者數，以形勝扼險，不可罷，乃內修屯務，外輯羌戎，因俗拊循，擇人為理，番眾相安者垂四十余年。 及宣德初，調兵啟釁，致動幹戈，自是置鎮建牙，宿重兵以資彈壓，亦時服時叛。 自漳臘以北即為大荒，斯籌邊者之所亟圖也。
Songpan was an isolated fortress in a remote land, its lifeline a single supply road through Longzhou—holding it was hard. Hongwu repeatedly considered abandoning it, but its strategic passes made withdrawal impossible; the court then built up garrison farms, rallied Qiang and Rong tribes, ruled through local custom, and chose capable men—so the frontier stayed quiet for nearly forty years. Early Xuande troop deployments provoked war; thereafter the Ming garrisoned Songpan in force, crushing rebels when needed—yet tribes still submitted and rebelled by turns. North of Zhangla lay only wilderness—the prize every frontier strategist coveted.
61
天全六番招討司
The Tianquan Six-Banner Pacification Commission
62
天全，古氐羌地。 五代孟蜀時，置碉門、黎、雅、長河西、魚通、寧遠六軍安撫司。 宋因之，隸雅州。 元置六安撫司，屬土番等處宣慰司，後改六番招討，又分置天全招討司。 明初並為天全六番招討司，隸四川都司。
Tianquan was ancient Di and Qiang country. Under Later Shu the court set up six army pacification offices: Diaomen, Li, Ya, Changxihe, Yutong, and Ningyuan. Song kept the arrangement, placing them under Ya prefecture. The Yuan created six pacification offices under the native-tribes pacification commission, later reorganized as the Six-Banner campaign commission with a separate Tianquan campaign office. Early Ming merged them into the Tianquan Six-Banner pacification commission under the Sichuan regional command.
63
洪武六年，天全六番招討使高英遣子敬嚴等來朝，貢方物。 帝賜以文綺龍衣。 以英為正招討，楊藏卜為副招討，秩從五品，每三歲入貢，賜予甚厚。 二十一年，楊藏卜來朝，言茶戶向與西番貿易，歲收其課。 近在官收買，額遂虧，乞從民便，許之。 先是，高敬嚴襲招討使，偕楊藏卜奏請簡土民為兵，以守邊境，詔許之。 敬嚴等遂招選土民，教以戰陣，得馬步卒千余人。 至是藏卜來朝，奏其事，詔更天全六番招討司為武職，令戍守邊界，控制西番。 三十一年，帝諭左都督徐增壽曰：「曩因碉門拒長河西口，道路險隘，以致往來跋涉艱難，市馬數少。 今聞有路自碉門出枯木任場徑抵長河西口，通雜道長官司，道路平坦，往來徑直，可即檄所司開拓，以便往來。」
In Hongwu 6 commissioner Gao Ying sent his son Jingyan to court with tribute. The emperor granted brocade and dragon robes. Ying became chief commissioner and Yang Cangbu vice commissioner at vice-fifth rank; they tribute every three years and received lavish gifts. In year 21 Yang Cangbu reported that tea households had long traded with western fan tribes and paid yearly levies on that commerce. Recent state monopsony had cut their income; he asked to restore private trade, and the court agreed. Earlier heir Gao Jingyan and Yang Cangbu had asked to draft native militia for border defense, and the throne approved. They recruited natives, drilled them in formation, and fielded 1,000-odd foot and horse troops. When Cangbu reported the force at court, the throne reclassified the Tianquan Six-Banner commission as a military post to garrison the frontier and watch the western fan. In year 31 the emperor told left regional commander Xu Zengshou: "(Diaomen once blocked access to the Changxihe mouth; the old road was so steep that traders struggled through and few horses reached market. We now hear of a level route from Diaomen through Kumurenchang straight to the Changxihe mouth and the Zadao chang office—order it opened at once for easier traffic.)"
64
永樂二年，高敬讓來朝，並賀立皇太子，且遣其子虎入國子學，賜虎衣衾等物。 十年，敬讓遣子虎貢馬。 初，虎入國學讀書，以丁母憂去，至是服闋還監，皇太子命禮部賜予如例。
In Yongle 2 Gao Jingrang came to court to congratulate the crown prince, sent his son Hu to the Imperial Academy, and received bedding and robes for the boy. In year 10 Jingrang sent Hu with horses as tribute. Hu had left the academy for his mother's mourning; now back after the mourning term, the crown prince ordered ritual gifts as usual.
65
宣德五年，六番招討司奏：「舊額歲辦烏茶五萬斤，二年一次，運付碉門茶馬司易馬。 今戶部令再辦芽茶二千二百斤，山深地瘠，艱於采辦，乞減其數。 」帝令免烏茶只辦芽茶。 十年命高鳳署天全六番招討司事。 先是，敬讓以罪下獄死。 至是，其子鳳乞襲父職。 帝念其祖有撫綏功，命暫理招討事。 正統四年命鳳襲。
In Xuande 5 the Six-Banner commission reported: "(Their old quota was 50,000 jin of brick tea every two years, delivered to the Diaomen tea-horse office for horses. The Revenue Board now demands another 2,200 jin of bud tea; the hills are poor and hard to harvest—please cut the levy. The emperor exempted brick tea and kept only the bud-tea quota. In year 10 Gao Feng was appointed acting commissioner of the Tianquan Six-Banner office. Earlier Jingrang had died in prison for a crime. Now his son Feng petitioned to inherit the post. Mindful of the grandfather's pacification service, the emperor let Feng manage the commission temporarily. In Zhengtong 4 Feng received formal succession.
66
正德十五年，招討高文林父子稱兵亂，副招討楊世仁亦助惡。 命四川撫按官討之。 初，文林等與蘆山縣民爭田構釁，知縣處置失宜，致叛亂。 逾年，討斬文林，擒其子繼恩，擇其宗人承襲。
In Zhengde 15 commissioner Gao Wenlin and his son raised troops; vice commissioner Yang Shiren joined the revolt. Sichuan's pacification and surveillance officials were ordered to suppress them. The trouble began when Wenlin clashed with Lushan farmers over land and the magistrate mishandled it into open revolt. A year later troops killed Wenlin, captured his son Jien, and installed a kinsman as heir.
67
初，天全招討司治碉門城，元之碉門安撫司也，在雅州境。 明初，宣慰余思聰、王德貴歸附，始降司為州，設雅州千戶所，而設碉門百戶，近天全六番之界。 又置茶課司以平互市。 蓋其地為南詔咽喉，三十六番朝貢出入之路。 三十六番者，皆西南諸部落，洪武初，先後至京，授職賜印。 立都指揮使二：曰烏斯藏，曰朵甘。 為宣慰司者三：曰朵甘，曰董卜韓胡，曰長河西魚通寧遠。 為招討司者六，為萬戶府者四，為千戶所者十七，是為三十六種。 或三年，或五年一朝貢，其道皆由雅州入，詳《西番傳》。
The Tianquan campaign office first sat at Diaomen city—the Yuan Diaomen pacification seat—in Ya prefecture. Early Ming pacification commissioners Yu Sicong and Wang Degui submitted; the office was demoted to a prefecture, Ya gained a thousand-household post, and a Diaomen centurion post was placed on the Tianquan Six-Banner frontier. A tea-tax office was added to regulate border trade. The place was Nanzhao's throat—the corridor through which thirty-six fan tribes brought tribute to court. Those thirty-six fan tribes were southwestern peoples who, in early Hongwu, came to court in turn for titles and seals. Two regional commands were created: U-Tsang and Do-kham. Three pacification commissions followed: Do-kham, Dongbu Hanhu, and Changxihe-Yutong-Ningyuan. Six pacification commissions, four wanhu offices, and seventeen qianhu posts made up the thirty-six jurisdictions. They tribute every three or five years, all entering through Ya—see the Western Fan treatise.
68
黎州，漢沈黎郡地。 《史記》稱越巂以東北，君長以十數，筰都最大。 自唐蒙通夜郎，邛、筰之君請為內臣，因置筰都縣，復曰旄牛縣。 元鼎中，以為沈黎郡。 唐割雅、巂二州置黎州。 天寶初，改為洪源郡，尋改漢源。 宋屬成都路。 元屬土番等處宣慰司。
Lizhou was the Han Shenli commandery. The Records say that east of northeast Yuexi dozens of chieftains ruled, Zuodu foremost among them. When Tang Meng opened Yelang, the Qiong and Zuodu lords asked to submit; the court set Zuodu county, later renamed Maoniu. Under Emperor Wu's Yuanding reign it became Shenli commandery. Tang detached land from Ya and Xi to form Lizhou. Early in Tianbao it became Hongyuan commandery, soon renamed Hanyuan. Under Song it belonged to Chengdu circuit. Under Yuan it fell under the native-tribes pacification commission.
69
洪武八年省漢源縣，置黎州長官司，以芍德為長官。 德，雲南人，馬姓。 祖仕元，世襲邛部州六番招討使。 明氏據蜀，德兄安復為黎州招討使。 明氏亡，蠻民潰散，德奉母還居邛部。 至是，四川布政司招之，德遂來朝貢馬，請置長官司。 詔以德為黎州長官，賜印及衣服綺帛，十一年升為黎州安撫司，即以德為使。 十四年，德遣使貢馬。 詔賜德鈔五十四錠、文綺七疋。 自是，三年一入貢。 弘治十四年命黎州安撫隸四川都司。
In Hongwu 8 the court abolished Hanyuan county and made Shaode Lizhou native magistrate. Shaode was a Yunnanese of the Ma clan. His family had served Yuan as hereditary Qiongbu Six-Banner commissioners. While the Ming Xia held Shu, his elder brother Anfu became Lizhou commissioner. When the Xia fell, the tribes scattered; Shaode brought his mother home to Qiongbu. The Sichuan administration then summoned him; Shaode came to court with horses and asked for a native office. The throne made him Lizhou magistrate with seal, robes, and silk; in year 11 the post became a pacification commission with Shaode as commissioner. In year 14 he sent envoys with horses. The court granted him fifty-four ingots of paper money and seven bolts of brocade. Thereafter he tribute every three years. In Hongzhi 14 Lizhou pacification was placed under the Sichuan regional command.
70
萬歷十九年，安撫馬祥無後，妻瞿氏掌司事，取瞿姓子撫之，將有他誌。 祥侄上舍居松坪者，遂興兵攻城，奪印，番眾乘機剽掠。 時參將吳文傑方有征東之役，移師剿平之。 二十四年降黎州安撫司為千戶所，立所治於司南三十里大田山壩。 分上七枝編戶，屬大渡河千戶所，下七枝仍屬松坪馬氏約束。 松坪在司之東南，自炒米城直接峨眉，高山峻阪三百餘里，皆安撫族人居之。
In Wanli 19 commissioner Ma Xiang died without heirs; his wife Lady Qu ran the office, adopted a Qu clansman, and plotted a new succession. A nephew in Songping raised troops, stormed the city, seized the seal, and fan tribes looted the countryside. Regional vice commander Wu Wenjie, then campaigning east, diverted his force and crushed the revolt. In year 24 Lizhou pacification became a qianhu post with its seat thirty li south at Datian mountain dam. The upper seven registered branches went to the Dadu River qianhu; the lower seven stayed under the Ma of Songping. Songping lay southeast of the commission—a 300-li march of high ridges from Chaomi city to Emei, all home to the commissioner's clan.
71
黎、雅諸蠻，宋時屢為邊患。 明興，以諸蠻皆天全六番諸部，散居於二州之境，遂於黎州設安撫，於天全六番設招討，以示羈縻。 而雅州所屬，與招討所轄之蠻民，境土相連，時有爭訟。 僥外大、小木瓜種分三枝，膩乃卜最強，世居西河。 初屬馬湖土官安氏鈐轄，自馬湖改流，諸瓜叛入邛部，歸嶺氏。 其地自西河至涼山、雪山諸處，周圍蟠據。 嘉靖末，諸瓜畜牧蕃盛，時窺邊，邛部長官嶺柏不能制，嘉、峨、犍為諸邊皆為侵擾。 鎮巡官督邛部兵捕之，瓜兵益熾，乃議大征，分建昌、越巂、馬湖三路兵進討。 瓜部始惶駭請降，願歲貢馬方物，乃定。 其地四千八百四十余畝，徵糧四百四十余石，輸峨眉縣。 明初與安撫司同置者，有大渡河守禦千戶所。 唐時，河平廣可通漕，戍將一不守，則黎、雅、邛、嘉、成都皆動搖。 宋建隆三年，王全斌平蜀，以圖來上。 議者欲因兵威復越巂，藝祖以玉斧畫圖曰：「外此，吾不有也。 」自是之後，河中流忽陷下五六十丈，水至此，洶湧如空中落，船筏不通，名為噎口，殆天設險以限內外雲。
Li and Ya tribes had been Song's chronic border trouble. At the dynasty's founding the court treated them as Tianquan Six-Banner peoples scattered across Li and Ya, setting a Lizhou pacification commission and a Tianquan Six-Banner campaign commission as tokens of indirect rule. Yazhou's jurisdictions and the tribes under the pacification commission shared borders and often quarreled over territory. Beyond Jiao, the great and lesser Mugua clans split into three lines; Ninabo was strongest and had long held the West River. They had once been subject to the An native officials of Mahu; after Mahu was placed under Han administrators, the Gua clans rebelled, fled into Qiongbu, and acknowledged the Ling chieftains. Their territory stretched from the West River to Liangshan and the snowy ranges, wrapping around the frontier in a great arc. By the late Jiajing era the Gua herds had grown vast; they raided the borders repeatedly. Ling Bai, chief of Qiongbu, could not restrain them, and Jia, Emeishan, and Qianwei suffered constant attacks. Frontier officials sent Qiongbu troops against them, but Gua resistance intensified; the court then mounted a major expedition, advancing in three columns from Jianchang, Yuexi, and Mahu. Terrified, the Gua submitted and pledged annual tribute of horses and local goods, and the matter was settled. Their registered fields exceeded four thousand eight hundred forty mu, taxed at more than four hundred forty shi of grain payable to Emei County. At the dynasty's founding a Dadu River defense qianhu office was set up alongside the pacification commission. Under the Tang the river was broad and calm enough for grain transport; lose a single garrison and Li, Ya, Qiong, Jia, and Chengdu would all quake. In Song Jianlong 3 Wang Quanbin completed the conquest of Shu and presented a map to the throne. Some urged using the army's momentum to recover Yuexi; the Founding Emperor traced the map with a jade axe and declared, "Beyond this, I want nothing." Thereafter the riverbed dropped fifty or sixty zhang; the current thundered as if falling from the sky, and no boat could pass—called the Choking Mouth, as if Heaven itself had barred the way between within and without.
